It was perhaps early evidence that in a series that is likely to be decided by fine margins, Milwaukee’s formidable bullpen might ultimately make the difference.Pat Murphy, the Brewers manager andBruce Springsteen superfanwho was FaceTimed by The Boss in midweek, declared Contreras the “player of the game” after he drove in a run and threw out two attempted base-stealers, neutralizing akey strategyfor Kevin Cash’s aggressive Rays.View image in fullscreenMilwaukee shortstop Cooper Pratt fails to complete a game-ending double play against Tampa Bay in Game 1 of the World Series on Friday night.Photograph: Ross Harried/EPA“Money isn’t everything” is a nice narrative as far as the action goes, but the peculiar genius of American sports is how they generally preserve parity and uncertainty on the field while embracing rapacious capitalism.Three years ago, the Brewers, who are owned byMark Attansio, a Los Angeles-based investor who also controls Norwich City FC and has an estimated net worth of $2bn, managed to squeeze$500m out of lawmakersin taxpayer-funded upgrades for a 25-year-old ballpark that cost less than $400m to build in the first place.A high-stakes financial duel engulfing the entire leagueplayed outto gaggles of reporters before the game as two power-brokers dug in to entrenched positions near the first-base dug-out. Bruce Meyer, the interim head of the players’ union, called the owners’ proposal of a salary cap a “nuclear bomb” and - more reasonably - argued that the presence of two small-market clubs in this year’s World Series proves that competitive balance is possible without a cap. Meanwhile, MLB commissioner Rob Manfred broadened the context as he made the case for a limit: “It’s been 40 years since we’re here. Once every 40 years is not enough. It’s not that no small market can win, it’s just that it’s pretty rare.”Milwaukee has a retractable roof, and Tampa Bay an indoor dome, but storm clouds are gathering above all the same. The owners are virtually certain to lock out the players on 1 December in a row over money that will threaten the start of the 2027 season. So this is a sport freighted with growing anxiety about the future, even during its showpiece event. Perhaps this, as well as the novelty factor of the match-up, is amplifying the party atmosphere of the last spectacle before the stoppage.Explore more on these topicsWorld SeriesMilwaukee BrewersTampa Bay RaysBaseballUS sportsfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: ‘Like a fairy tale’: USA’s Paula Moltzan becomes oldest first-time World Cup winner by 0.01sec | Skiing | The Guardian
description: The American skier produced a stunning second run to claim her maiden World Cup victory, edging Albania’s Lara Colturi by just one-hundredth of a second
Author: Bryan Armen Graham
Headline: The American skier produced a stunning second run to claim her maiden World Cup victory, edging Albania’s Lara Colturi by just one-hundredth of a second
Content: Paula Moltzan celebrates after claiming her first career World Cup victory in the women’s giant slalom at Sölden, Austria, on Saturday.Photograph: Gian Ehrenzeller/EPAView image in fullscreenPaula Moltzan celebrates after claiming her first career World Cup victory in the women’s giant slalom at Sölden, Austria, on Saturday.Photograph: Gian Ehrenzeller/EPASkiing‘Like a fairy tale’: USA’s Paula Moltzan becomes oldest first-time World Cup winner by 0.01secAmerican, 32, wins season-opening giant slalomMoltzan edges Albania’s Lara Colturi by 0.01secMikaela Shiffrin drops from first to seventh placeBryan Armen GrahamSat 24 Oct 2026 09.07 EDTLast modified on Sat 24 Oct 2026 19.34 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAmerican Paula Moltzan became the oldest woman to claim her first Alpine skiing World Cup victory on Saturday, pipping Albania’s Lara Colturi by just one-hundredth of a second in a thrilling season-opening giant slalom at Sölden, Austria.Moltzan, who was fifth after the opening run, produceda superb second descentto finish with a combined time of 2min 14.82sec, narrowly denying her Italian-born Albanian rival, who finished in 2min 14.83sec. Germany’s Emma Aicher completed the podium, 0.52sec behind the Minnesota native.“It feels like a fairy tale right now,” Moltzan said afterward. “Pretty unreal and I think it will take a minute to settle in.”The victory marked a long-sought breakthrough for Moltzan, who debuted on ski racing’s top flight in 2012 andwas dropped from the US teama decade ago. The 32-year-old, whowon an Olympic bronze in the team combined eventat the Milano Cortina Games in February, had finished second or third in 10 previous World Cup races across 13 seasons without ever reaching the top step of the podium.Starting the second run in fifth place, the American clocked 1min 7.86sec in increasingly foggy conditions to move four spots up the standings and set a target that none of the remaining contenders could beat.View image in fullscreenPaula Moltzan competes during the first run of the women’s giant slalom at the Alpine skiing World Cup in Sölden, Austria, on Saturday.Photograph: Johann Groder/APA/AFP/Getty Images“In the second run I knew I had to send it,” Moltzan said. “A lot of people tend to back off when it gets dark and, for me, I just want to push harder. It’s just an opportunity to be brave and take a chance.”She added: “You have to kind of fake it till you make it. And yeah, I guess I faked it well enough today.”The 19-year-old Colturi, who had been sixth after the opening run, came agonizingly close to denying Moltzan her moment, crossing 0.01sec behind the winning time to come up short by the slimmest of margins.Aicher also made a significant move, climbing from ninth after the first run to third, while Sweden’s Sara Hector slipped from second to fourth, 0.63sec off the pace.Moltzan’s American teammateMikaela Shiffrin, seeking a record-extending 111th World Cup victory, had led after the opening run but struggled amid the deteriorating visibility, sliding wide on one turn, and fell to seventh overall, 0.83sec behind the winner.Shiffrin, who equalled the women’s recordwith her sixth overall World Cup titlein March, has described the new campaign as an “exploration season” in which she plans to race less frequently in her signature slalom discipline to concentrate on giant slalom and super-G. The 31-year-old has not won a giant slalom race since December 2023, despite holding the women’s record with 22 career victories in the discipline.Saturday’s race also saw the return of Slovakia’s Petra Vlhová, the2022 Olympic slalom championand 2021 overall World Cup winner, who finished 23rd in her first appearance on the World Cup circuitsince January 2024following a 33-month injury layoff.Italy’s Federica Brignone, whowon Olympic gold in giant slalom and super-Gon home snow in February, was absent as she continues her recovery from surgery in August.For Moltzan, the result represented an immediate reward for a bold late-career equipment change. In May, she ended an 18-year association with French manufacturer Rossignol to join Van Deer–Red Bull Sports, becoming the first woman to race for the Austrian brand, which had previously supplied only male skiers.View image in fullscreenPaula Moltzan (center) celebrates her first career World Cup victory alongside runner-up Lara Colturi of Albania (left) and third-place finisher Emma Aicher of Germany after the women’s giant slalom in Sölden, Austria, on Saturday.Photograph: Alexis Boichard/Agence Zoom/Getty Images“I’ve been working a really long time for my first victory, but also, I never would have expected it would have happened first race on new material,” Moltzan said. “I guess it just proves that we’re doing something right.”The result also gave the United States two skiers inside the top seven, with AJ Hurt finishing 13th, Elisabeth Bocock 14th and Nina O’Brien tied for 16th. It also made Moltzan the first American woman other than Shiffrin to win a World Cup tech race sinceLindsey Vonnclaimed giant slalom gold in Åre, Sweden, in December 2015.Moltzan has also been making headlines away from the slopes. In an interview with the Athleticpublished on Friday, she discussed her campaign to expand fertility treatment coverage for US Olympic athletes, a cause she has promoted by racing with a floral uterus design on her helmet.The Minnesotan has argued that female athletes should not have to choose between pursuing their sporting ambitions and starting families, and is pushing for greater fertility benefits through theUS Olympic and Paralympic Committee.For now, Moltzan has every reason to savor the biggest victory of her career, achieved on the Rettenbach glacier slope in the traditional opening race of the World Cup season. “I can’t imagine a better start,” she said. “I’m really, really, really excited and I can’t wait to see everybody who’s here cheering us on.”Explore more on these topicsSkiingUS sportsMikaela ShiffrinUnited States Olympic & Paralympic Committee (USOPC)Lindsey VonnShareReuse this content

title: Alonso urges Cole Palmer ‘to learn’ from red card in Chelsea’s defeat to Spurs | Chelsea | The Guardian
description: The Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso said that Cole Palmer must learn from his red card during the shock 2-0 Premier League defeat to Tottenham at Stamford Bridge
Author: Jacob Steinberg
Headline: The Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso said that Cole Palmer must learn from his red card during the shock 2-0 Premier League defeat to Tottenham at Stamford Bridge
Content: Cole Palmer is shown a red card by Chris Kavanagh.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianView image in fullscreenCole Palmer is shown a red card by Chris Kavanagh.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/The GuardianChelseaAlonso urges Cole Palmer ‘to learn’ from red card in Chelsea’s defeat to SpursForward sent off after 80 minutes for second yellow card‘We need to have maturity to deal with difficult moments’Jacob Steinbergat Stamford BridgeSat 24 Oct 2026 16.19 EDTLast modified on Sat 24 Oct 2026 16.28 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleXabi Alonso said that Cole Palmer must learn from his red card during Chelsea’sshock 2-0 defeat to Tottenham, who claimed their first win at Stamford Bridge since 2018 thanks to an own goal from Mike Penders and a late effort from Mathys Tel.Tottenham stun Chelsea for second league win in a week as Cole Palmer is sent offRead moreSpurs, who had won on one of their previous 34 trips to west London, were already 1-0 up when Palmer earned a second yellow card for catching Conor Gallagher with a late tackle. The playmaker could have been sent off earlier – his first booking came during a clash with Mateus Fernandes – and Alonso agreed that this could be an important lesson for the 24-year-old.“Absolutely,” Chelsea’s manager said. “I haven’t seen them [back] on TV but as far as I have been told probably he [the referee] got it right. We need to have this maturity to deal with difficult moments. When you have conceded for 1-0, still probably it was 15-20 minutes to go. I need to check the action to talk with Cole but it is one to learn for the future for sure.”View image in fullscreenCole Palmer clashes with Mateus Fernandes, earning his first yellow card.Photograph: Isabel Infantes/ReutersAlonso said there are no wider concerns with Palmer’s character, even though Chelsea’s No 10 could have been sent offagainst Everton last weekendtoo. “Today, for sure, yes, but it is not a concern,” Alonso said. “It is a moment to keep calm, a moment to keep mature, for everyone.”Chelsea struggled without João Pedro and do not know when the forward will return after picking up an unspecified injury in training on Friday. “He has a lot of fluid,” Alonso said. “He felt it yesterday and we need to wait to do the test and to know the whole seriousness of the injury.”Alonso defended Penders after the goalkeeper punched a corner into his own net on his full Premier League debut. “We win, we lose together,” he said. “We support Mike and we support the rest of the team. He will learn from that.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionRoberto De Zerbi hopes that Spurs can use this victory as a springboard. “Why not?” the Spurs manager said. “There is no reason why not. I can’t understand why we have to ask this question. Because we won two games in a row. But we didn’t win nothing. We want to improve, improve and improve, to be better game by game, week by week. I think we have suffered enough.”Explore more on these topicsChelseaTottenham HotspurXabi AlonsonewsShareReuse this content

title: Rising US star Fred Richard wins first world gymnastics title as Skye Blakely adds two more medals | Gymnastics | The Guardian
description: Richard becomes the first American man to win a world floor title since 2003 as Blakely takes her medal haul to four in Rotterdam
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: Richard becomes the first American man to win a world floor title since 2003 as Blakely takes her medal haul to four in Rotterdam
Content: Frederick Richard celebrates on the podium after winning gold in the men’s floor exercise final at the world gymnastics championships in Rotterdam on Saturday.Photograph: Piroschka Van De Wouw/ReutersView image in fullscreenFrederick Richard celebrates on the podium after winning gold in the men’s floor exercise final at the world gymnastics championships in Rotterdam on Saturday.Photograph: Piroschka Van De Wouw/ReutersGymnasticsRising US star Fred Richard wins first world gymnastics title as Skye Blakely adds two more medalsAmerican, 22, edges Britain’s Jake Jarman by 0.033Blakely takes vault and bars bronze after all-around goldSimone Biles watches as Americans shine in RotterdamGuardian sportand agenciesSat 24 Oct 2026 10.06 EDTLast modified on Sat 24 Oct 2026 15.19 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAmerican Frederick Richard won the floor exercise title at the world gymnastics championships in Rotterdam on Saturday, finishing ahead of Britain’s Jake Jarman and Israel’s Artem Dolgopyat.Skye Blakely caps remarkable injury comeback with world gymnastics all-around titleRead moreWith US gymnastics greatSimone Bileslooking on as a spectator in the Netherlands, the 22-year-old Richard secured his first world title, edging out Jarman by just 0.033 points after scoring 14.633. Jarman, the defending world champion, was among a field that included the last two Olympic gold medallists.“I hope this is a lesson to everybody that you don’t have to wait to get the win to say you will be a champion,” Richard said afterward. “You don’t have to know when it’s going to happen or how it’s going to happen, but believing it every second of every day does pay off. I’m proof of that now.”Richard became the first American man to win a world title on floor exercise since Paul Hamm shared gold in 2003. He is also the first American man since Danell Leyva to win medals across team, all-around and individual apparatus events at the Olympics and world championships.View image in fullscreenFrederick Richard competes in the men’s floor exercise final at the world gymnastics championships in Rotterdam on Saturday, where he won his first world title.Photograph: Piroschka Van De Wouw/ReutersRichard, who won bronze in the all-around event at the 2023 world championships in Antwerp, also helped the United States win team bronze at the Paris 2024 Olympic Games.Elsewhere on Saturday, Newly minted all-around champion Skye Blakely added to her medal haul in Rotterdam, earning bronze on vault and uneven bars during the event finals on Saturday.The 21-year-old from Dallas, whosoared to gold in the all-around on Friday after recovering from injuries that wrecked her Olympic hopes in 2021 and again in 2024, hardly looked tired in what has quickly become the meet of her life.Blakely averaged a score of 14.166 on her pair of vaults to share the podium with gold medalist Rebeca Andrade of Brazil and American teammate Claire Pease.View image in fullscreenSkye Blakely of the United States competes in the women’s uneven bars final at the world gymnastics championships in Rotterdam on Saturday.Photograph: Tom Weller/Getty ImagesAndrade, the Olympic champion on vault and the Olympic silver medalist in the all-around in Paris behind Biles, edged Pease for gold. The 27-year-old Andrade, who is competing as an event specialist at the moment while eyeing a run at the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics, averaged 14.666, a bit ahead of Pease at 14.233.Kaylia Nemour of Algeria recovered from a misstep on vault in the all-around finals on Friday that cost her a medal to easily defend her gold on uneven bars. Nemour’s intricate and technically demanding routine – perhaps the hardest currently being done by any gymnast, male or female, on any event – earned her a 15.333, the highest score of the day.Helen Kervic of Germany captured the silver at 14.833, with Blakely in third at 14.600.Blakely, who joined Olympic champions Biles and Nastia Liukin as well as Rebecca Bross as the only American women to win at least four medals at a single worlds, will have a chance to add to her medal total on Sunday when she competes in the beam final.Explore more on these topicsGymnasticsSimone BilesUS sportsShareReuse this content

title: NFL shutters Paris fan experience as protests overshadow first France game | NFL | The Guardian
description: The NFL has closed fan attractions in Paris amid security concerns and planned protests ahead of Sunday’s historic Saints-Steelers game at Stade de France
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The NFL has closed fan attractions in Paris amid security concerns and planned protests ahead of Sunday’s historic Saints-Steelers game at Stade de France
Content: Former NFL player Donte Stallworth takes part in a Hail Mary throwing challenge on the banks of the Seine in Paris on Friday, ahead of Sunday’s game between the Saints and Steelers.Photograph: Dave Shopland/APView image in fullscreenFormer NFL player Donte Stallworth takes part in a Hail Mary throwing challenge on the banks of the Seine in Paris on Friday, ahead of Sunday’s game between the Saints and Steelers.Photograph: Dave Shopland/APNFLNFL shutters Paris fan experience as protests overshadow first France gameNFL House and city-center shop closed on SaturdayParis braces for protests amid heavy police presenceLive: Thousands march in Paris and other French citiesAgenciesSat 24 Oct 2026 12.55 EDTLast modified on Sat 24 Oct 2026 13.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe NFL closed its “NFL House” inParison Saturday as the city braced for street protests with a heavy police presence and storefronts boarded up.The league announced the closure to fans on Saturday morning through its “OnePass” app, a day after saying its pop-upNFLshop would also be shut on Saturday – in both cases citing “potential accessibility issues”.Aaron Rodgers says NFL’s Paris game is safe despite PSG cancellation amid unrestRead moreSecurity concerns have overshadowed the NFL’s debut in Paris. The New Orleans Saints will play thePittsburgh Steelerson Sunday at Stade de France in the league’s first regular-season game in France.Also on Saturday, the Saints announced that “Saints House has been postponed until Sunday.”Events planned for Saturday at NFL House included “French Athletes in Football” and “From the Field to the Community”.“I was looking forward to just checking out some of the installations they had – they were going to have the Lombardi Trophy,” fan Nick Paiva said.Major museums, including the Louvre and the Musée d’Orsay, were closed on Saturday, though tourists lined up to enter Notre Dame Cathedral. French authorities were intent on preventing a repeat of recent violent unrest.The disorder has also disrupted French football, with Sunday’s Ligue 1 match between Paris Saint-Germain and Lyon postponed until Monday at the request of local police, who cited security concerns and the strain on resources.The US state department issued a security alert this week cautioning “Americans in Paris for the NFL game” to “exercise caution and be aware of their surroundings” because of protests.View image in fullscreenNFL France general manager Matthieu Maignal speaks at a press conference in Paris on Monday ahead of the league’s first regular-season game in France between the Steelers and Saints.Photograph: Johnny Fidelin/Icon Sport/Getty ImagesNFL commissionerRoger Goodellsaid this week that preparations had been made in consultation with US and French authorities. Street protests, he said, “are not unusual in France”.Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgerssaid on Fridaythat he was confident the game would go ahead as planned. “I definitely think that the NFL is alert to what’s going on,” the four-time MVP said. “This game means a lot to the NFL. If it was unsafe, then I’m sure we wouldn’t be here.”Thousands march in Paris and other French cities as protests take place across Europe – Europe liveRead moreOn Friday, French presidentEmmanuel Macronmet Goodell, Saints owner Gayle Benson and Steelers owner Art Rooney II at the Élysée Palace to “discuss Sunday’s game and the long-term future of the NFL in Paris”.The NFL said on Friday that its pop-up shop in the city center would be closed on Saturday but that fans could use an alternative shop at Stade deFrance, north of the city in Saint-Denis.A weekend event for Steelers fans was canceled on Thursday because of security concerns.Paiva, an American who lives in France, wanted to visit NFL House, where his French partner could learn more about the sport.He had also expected to participate in the league’s “Hail Mary over the Seine” activation, in which fans try to throw a football across the famed waterway near Notre Dame. Despite having registered, Paiva was told at the site that he also needed to have reserved a time slot.“That was not communicated very well,” he said after being turned away. “C’est comme ça – it’s the way it is.”French teenager Oskar Le Gall, wearing a Bryce Young jersey, was able to give it a shot. His throw came up a little short. A worker on the other side stayed busy scooping balls out of the river with a long pole fitted with a net.View image in fullscreenThe NFL announced that its pop-up store in central Paris would be closed on Saturday amid concerns over planned street protests ahead of Sunday’s game.Photograph: Johnny Fidelin/Icon Sport/Getty ImagesLe Gall, who is from Brittany, said “the atmosphere of the NFL in Paris is amazing”, noting that French sports leagues and teams typically do not promote themselves as extensively.Le Gall and his brother were keeping an eye on the planned route of Saturday’s protests.“It doesn’t feel calm and good to be a tourist in Paris,” he said. “It’s not good for the NFL.”At one point during the Hail Mary event, 11 national police vans with their emergency lights flashing drove past on the street above as a fan prepared to throw a ball.Steelers fan Monika Allen was able to avoid any protests thanks to advice posted in fan-led Facebook groups.“The fans are doing a good job keeping each other informed of where to be and where not to be,” Allen said near the Hail Mary event.Her cousin, Viktor Toth, was wearing her black Terry Bradshaw Steelers jersey.“We’re not worried,” she said. “My cousin is Hungarian, so he knows that the protests happen regularly in Paris.”Explore more on these topicsNFLPittsburgh SteelersNew OrleansParisFranceRoger GoodellEmmanuel MacronShareReuse this content

title: Nashville SC seal first MLS Supporters’ Shield with 2-0 win over CF Montreal | Nashville SC | The Guardian
description: Sam Surridge and Hany Mukhtar scored second-half goals as Nashville SC beat CF Montreal 2-0 to claim the Supporters’ Shield for the first time
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Sam Surridge and Hany Mukhtar scored second-half goals as Nashville SC beat CF Montreal 2-0 to claim the Supporters’ Shield for the first time
Content: Hany Mukhtar celebrates scoring Nashville SC’s second goal during their 2-0 win over CF Montreal at Saputo Stadium on Saturday, a victory that secured the club’s first MLS Supporters’ Shield.Photograph: Tim Austen/MLS/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenHany Mukhtar celebrates scoring Nashville SC’s second goal during their 2-0 win over CF Montreal at Saputo Stadium on Saturday, a victory that secured the club’s first MLS Supporters’ Shield.Photograph: Tim Austen/MLS/Getty ImagesNashville SCNashville SC seal first MLS Supporters’ Shield with 2-0 win over CF MontrealSurridge and Mukhtar fire Nashville to 2-0 victoryNashville extend unbeaten streak to seven matchesMontreal teenager Keita impresses on MLS debutAgenciesSat 24 Oct 2026 17.07 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleNashville SC scored twice in the second half to claim the Supporters’ Shield as the top team in MLS with a 2-0 win at CF Montreal on Saturday.The win allowed Nashville (21-3-7, 70 points) to stretch their unbeaten streak to seven games (5-0-2).Montreal (6-18-7, 25 points) have just one win in their past 11 games (1-8-2) and have been officially eliminated from playoff contention.Removing political speech from MLS fans is untenable – just ask Austin FCRead moreSam Surridge buried his own rebound to give Nashville a 1-0 lead in the 52nd minute. Montreal goalkeeper Samsy Keita, the 17-year-old homegrown player making hisMLSdebut, denied Surridge’s header from the right side of the goal area off a cross from Reed Baker-Whiting. The rebound went right to Surridge, who easily put it into the far side for his team-leading 18th goal of the season.Hany Mukhtar made it 2-0 in the 76th minute. He intercepted defender Brayan Vera’s clearing attempt outside the box, was first to it as it rolled inside the box and then hit a shot that deflected off Keita and into the net from the top right corner of the goal area.Mukhtar nearly tied Surridge atop the Nashville scoring charts with an attempt inside the box in the 80th minute, but Keita got his hands up to deflect it away.Keita was tested early in the first half, coming off his line to the penalty spot to deny Surridge an opportunity late in the second minute.That was all either side would generate offensively in a slow start, with just one shot attempted between the two teams through the first 18 minutes.Montreal started to find their game as the half progressed but couldn’t convert.Vera’s header off a corner from the left side in the 21st minute just missed the far post. Ten minutes later, Nashville goalkeeper Brian Schwake easily snared a free kick off the foot of Alexis Sanchez and 90 seconds later got in front of an opportunity from Hennadii Synchuk.In the 33rd minute, Dante Sealy came down the left side on a rush but sent the ball over the net.Explore more on these topicsNashville SCMLSCF MontréalUS sportsShareReuse this content

title: Clinical Arsenal earn precious win against Everton thanks to Konsa and Gabriel | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Arsenal moved level on points with Manchester City at the top after Ezri Konsa and Gabriel Magalhães scored in a 2-0 home win against Everton
Author: Ed Aarons
Headline: Arsenal moved level on points with Manchester City at the top after Ezri Konsa and Gabriel Magalhães scored in a 2-0 home win against Everton
Content: Gabriel Magalhães directs his header home, despite Kai Havertz jumping in front of him, to make it 2-0 to Arsenal.Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenGabriel Magalhães directs his header home, despite Kai Havertz jumping in front of him, to make it 2-0 to Arsenal.Photograph: Matthew Childs/Action Images/ReutersPremier LeagueClinical Arsenal earn precious win against Everton thanks to Konsa and GabrielEd Aaronsat the Emirates StadiumSat 24 Oct 2026 12.03 EDTLast modified on Sat 24 Oct 2026 14.06 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe wait goes on for David Moyes. The 63-year-old Scot must have been hoping that on his 14th visit to this stadium as Everton’s manager, his luck would change. Yet from the moment Ezri Konsa slammed home his first goal for Arsenal as thePremier Leaguechampions rediscovered their knack of scoring from set pieces, the writing was on the wall.While it took until midway through the second half for Gabriel Magalhães to make sure of the victory, Arsenal were never going to let slip the chance of moving level on points at the top with Manchester Cityafter their defeat by Aston Villaearlier in the day.Fulham climb out of drop zone after Oscar Bobb’s late show sinks CoventryRead moreAsked whether it was strange that his side are again going toe-to-toe with their great rivals but with the added uncertainty of what punishment City will receive after being foundguilty of 115 chargesby the Premier League, Mikel Arteta said: “[We are] just focusing on what we can do. We are very pleased with 90% of the results and performances that we have.”This was hardly a vintage performance from the clinical home side after a testing week but it did not need to be against opponents who offered precious little in attack, even if they defended for their lives at times.Having gone six matches without defeat to start the season, a second in succession will only add to Everton’s concerns after confirmation that the club’s American owners want out.“It was always going to be hard after conceding the early goal,” said Moyes, whose solitary victory at the Emirates was as West Ham’s manager in 2023. “I want us to challenge the top teams but it’s difficult when you see the strength of their bench.”Everton’s record at this stadium is almost as bad as their manager’s. They arrived in north London having won twice in 35 matches here and had to do without Jarrad Branthwaite and Jack Grealish, who was ruled out with illness. It did not bode well for them whenArsenaltook the lead in the seventh minute with a third corner in succession.View image in fullscreenEzri Konsa (No 15) squeezes the ball home for Arsenal’s early first goal against Everton.Photograph: Adam Davy/PAGabriel made the crucial first contact at the near post and Jordan Pickford tipped the ball on to the crossbar, only for Vitaliy Mykolenko’s failed clearance under pressure from Viktor Gyökeres to allow Konsa to ram home from close range. After a record-breaking 25 goals from set pieces last season, it was their first of this campaign.It was a measure ofArsenal’s exertions against Bayern Munichon Wednesday that Arteta rotated his side more than usual for a Premier League match, making five changes.Eberechi Eze and Noni Madueke spurned good opportunities to extend the lead in front of the watching England head coach, Thomas Tuchel. The latter was left out of the last squad, but could well benefit from Bukayo Saka’s expected long absence due to a thigh injury. He was inches away with an instinctive effort with his right foot from the edge of the area on the half-hour mark and was consistently Arsenal’s most dangerous threat.Everton must have feared the worst as yet another Arsenal corner – 10 during the first half – was launched into the area. Yet the defence just about stood firm.A moment’s lapse of concentration from Ben White just before half-time almost gave Everton an equaliser but Thierno Barry could not get enough on his attempt to flick the ball past David Raya in their clearest opening.Gyökeres looked determined to make an impression on his first Premier League start of the season but the Sweden striker, who has yet to score for his club this term, looked laboured.Quick GuideArsenal 2-0 Everton key factsShow• With both Arsenal and Manchester City doing so this season, this is just the third top-flight campaign to havetwo teams win at least seven of their opening eight matchesafter 1892-93 (Preston and Sunderland) and 1913-14 (Blackburn and Manchester United).• This was David Moyes’s400th defeatacross all competitions in his managerial career with all clubs.31of thesehave come against Arsenal, more than against any other opponent.• The opener from Ezri Konsa (pictured celebrating) was Arsenal’sfirst set piece goal(excluding penalties)since Mayagainst Crystal Palace, ending a run of 13 games without one.OptaPhotograph: Adam Davy/PAWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.He could not believe it when Tony Harrington penalised him for a foul on James Tarkowski and a sheepish Arteta earned himself a booking for protesting. Unsurprisingly, Gyökeres’ number was up soon after as Arsenal turned to their bench.It took less than 60 seconds for Gabriel to head in at the back post as White offered Tuchel a timely reminder of his qualities with a brilliant cross.Moyes’ frustration meant he joined Arteta in the referee’s notebook. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall could have made things interesting but his header fizzed just wide of a post.Arsenal are now breathing down City’s necks, although whether this title race lasts the course remains unknown.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueArsenalEvertonmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Fulham climb out of drop zone after Oscar Bobb’s late show sinks Coventry | Premier League | The Guardian
description: The Norwegian winger scored in the 80th minute to earn Fulham a vital 1-0 win against Coventry, who are now second-bottom in the Premier League
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The Norwegian winger scored in the 80th minute to earn Fulham a vital 1-0 win against Coventry, who are now second-bottom in the Premier League
Content: Oscar Bobb shows his delight after scoring Fulham’s winner.Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/ReutersView image in fullscreenOscar Bobb shows his delight after scoring Fulham’s winner.Photograph: Peter Cziborra/Action Images/ReutersPremier LeagueFulham climb out of drop zone after Oscar Bobb’s late show sinks CoventryPress AssociationSat 24 Oct 2026 12.11 EDTLast modified on Sat 24 Oct 2026 14.33 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleOscar Bobb’s firstPremier Leaguegoal for Fulham earned a win against Coventry that lifted Álvaro Arbeloa’s side clear of the relegation zone.Bobb produced a fine bit of individual skill to score in the 80th minute, twisting his way into the area and bending a shot into the far corner. It was his second goal for the club since his £27m move from Manchester City in January.Clinical Arsenal earn precious win against Everton thanks to Konsa and GabrielRead moreThat was enough to give Fulham their first away win in nine attempts, a run that dated back to February, a week after they ended their winless start to the league campaign bybeating Hull 1-0.Josh King had earlier hit the post for the visitors, who edged Coventry in just about every department to leave Frank Lampard’s team second-bottom of the table.The hosts had only brief spells of sustained possession in Fulham’s half, but did little to trouble Bernd Leno on a frustrating afternoon that bought the Coventry fans back down to earth after their4-1 win against Newcastlein their previous home match.“I think we are improving as a team,” Arbeloa said. “We are competing for 90 minutes. I talked to the players. It’s not about if we play well for 60 minutes or 30 minutes, we need to understand that you need to compete for 90 minutes.“Understand the game, understand what you have to do. Sometimes you need to defend your box, sometimes you will control the game.“Sometimes you need to win because of the quality of your players. I think it was a good game as a team but at the end the quality of Oscar in one moment decides the game.”Quality was in short supply between two teams who started the day in the bottom three. King should have broken the deadlock in the 18th minute when afforded too much space in the box, but his powerful shot rebounded off the top of the upright before Alex Iwobi sent a wild follow-up effort high and wide.At the other end, Bobby Thomas met Jack Rudoni’s free-kick but got his angles all wrong as he headed well wide, before Brandon Thomas-Asante missed from Jay Dasilva’s cross after a good run forward from Rudoni.A mis-hit back pass from Antonee Robinson offered Thomas-Asante another chance but his shot lacked power as Leno easily gathered.View image in fullscreenEphron Mason-Clark is denied by the Fulham goalkeeper Bernd Leno.Photograph: Paul Currie/ShutterstockWhile Coventry were piling up half-chancesFulhamwere the ones bossing possession but, in keeping with their season so far, struggling to turn that dominance into goals. The Coventry defender Milan van Ewijk almost helped them out, deflecting Robinson’s low cross dangerously close to his own goal as it found the side-netting.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionJust before the break Calvin Bassey went down in the box claiming a shirt-pull from Thomas-Asante, but the referee Adam Herczeg waved play on with replays suggesting they each had a hold of the other.The video assistant referee had taken a look, and was involved again early in the second half when Rudoni’s free-kick from the right struck Iwobi on the arm before he cleared, but the Nigerian’s arms were by his side and play was waved on.Coventry then suffered a major blow when the in-form Thomas, praised by Lampard in midweek, hobbled off just before the hour, replaced by the teenage Manchester City loanee Stephen Mfuni.The hosts were starting to build some momentum after a series of substitutions but it swiftly ended as Bobb struck with 10 minutes to go.Coventry tried to respond but a powerful strike from Matt Grimes was blocked and a late penalty appeal for handball against Shea Charles was waved away with the midfielder having had his arm tucked in.“If it ends 0-0, I think both say fair play,” Lampard said. “Fulham are a good team, they’ve been creating a lot of chances – you can see why. They didn’t give us massive problems around our box but they found a moment of quality that we couldn’t find.“We didn’t have any real zip at the top end of the pitch, so that’s disappointing. Sometimes it can happen. This is the Premier League. They’re trying to stop you and if you want more it’s not always there. We’ve got to keep pushing on.”Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueCoventry CityFulhammatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Relief for Slegers as Russo rescues Arsenal against Tottenham in WSL  | Women's Super League | The Guardian
description: Arsenal recorded their first WSL win since the opening day of the season as they came from behind to beat Tottenham 2-1 in the north London derby
Author: Suzanne Wrack
Headline: Arsenal recorded their first WSL win since the opening day of the season as they came from behind to beat Tottenham 2-1 in the north London derby
Content: Alessia Russo sets off in celebration after her penalty sealed Arsenal’s fightback against Spurs in the WSL north London derby.Photograph: Keeran Marquis/KDMP/SPP/ShutterstockView image in fullscreenAlessia Russo sets off in celebration after her penalty sealed Arsenal’s fightback against Spurs in the WSL north London derby.Photograph: Keeran Marquis/KDMP/SPP/ShutterstockWomen's Super LeagueRelief for Slegers as Russo rescues Arsenal against Tottenham in WSLSuzanne Wrackat Tottenham Hotspur StadiumSat 24 Oct 2026 09.59 EDTLast modified on Sat 24 Oct 2026 14.55 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleAlessia Russo’s contentious second-half penalty delivered relief, a reprieve and a chance for a reset as Arsenal came from a goal down to earn their second win of the WSL season in the north London derby.Tottenham host Arsenal in WSL, Premier League, EFL and more – football clockwatch liveRead moreAt a rain-lashed Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, the Gunners were again their own worst enemy, forced to come from behind after Cathinka Tandberg’s headed opener. Georgia Stanway levelled and Russo powered in the penalty that gave them the lead they protected defiantly.The Tottenham manager, Martin Ho, queried the penalty decision, with the ball hitting the raised arm of substitute Ella Morris from the clearance of one of her teammates. “My interpretation of the rule is if your teammate hits it and it hits your player, if you’re one yard away, the time and distance is taken into account, so there’s no penalty,” he said. “That’s my understanding of it, from when we were told to start the season. I want to understand what they’re saying, because then I can accept the decision.“I don’t want the game to be about that, but when it decides a game it’s frustrating because it’s not within the law of the game.”Arsenal’s manager, Renée Slegers, said she was glad to give the fans a win. “They sing us and fight us through the game,” she said. “At the end it’s scrappy, it’s game management and it’s scenarios, and they’re all with us.”With the pressure building on her and her players after five games without a win, at times it felt like they were trying to disprove the phrase “you can’t dig yourself out of a hole”.Quick GuideBrighton cruise to victory against West HamShowMaisie Symonds’ first-half stunner sentBrightonon their way to a 3-0 win againstWestHamat the Amex Stadium. The midfielder Symonds’ thunderbolt gave the Seagulls a half-time lead before Fran Kirby and Kiko Seike struck quickfire goals midway through the second period. It was a first clean sheet this season for Arturo Ruiz’s side and lifts them up to eighth in the table, two points above West Ham, who slipped to 12th after their fifth league defeat of the campaign.Press AssociationWas this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.Arsenal had looked a little shaky in the opening few minutes but they settled, built possession and started to pose a threat. A failure to carve out clearcut chances and capitalise on any period of dominance has been the running theme of their season. They lacked fight and there was sloppiness too, with too many overhit passes putting the ball out of play or giving away possession.That the opener came from a Tottenham corner was unsurprising. Victoria Pelova swung the ball in and Tandberg rose above her two markers, Stanway and Emily Fox, who failed to even to jump and challenge, and headed home.Spurs’ joy was short lived as Stanway made up for her marking error four minutes later by arriving to meet Russo’s cut back and powered the ball in off the crossbar.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionView image in fullscreenGeorgia Stanway equalises for Arsenal in the 17th minute.Photograph: John Sibley/Action Images/ReutersAfter the break there was concern for Tottenham when Alice Sombath’s leg seemed to twist awkwardly as she stretched for the ball. The club’s record signing left on a stretcher to be replaced by Morris, who made her return from an anterior cruciate ligament injury towards the end of last season.After the lengthy stoppage, Russo forced a huge save from Lize Kop as she attempted to turn in Caitlin Foord’s cross from close range, the forward putting her hands to her head and screaming in frustration at the missed opportunity.It did not take long for that frustration to transform into elation. The resulting corner from Kyra Cooney-Cross was headed on by Leah Williamson at the near post and Lisa Baum’s effort came back off the post. Spurs’ clearance bounced off the raised arm of Morris and the referee pointed to the spot. Russo sent Kop the wrong way and drove the ball low into the corner.Arsenal were clinging on as the final whistle loomed but they had “found their fight,” said Slegers. “We had a run of games where results haven’t been good enough. It was frustrating for everyone. I’m so happy we got to win on this occasion, in the north London derby, away from home in the rain and we showed that character in the team.“This will definitely energise us. We need to back this up in the next couple of games.”Explore more on these topicsWomen's Super LeagueTottenham Hotspur WomenArsenal WomenWomen's footballmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Maresca ‘not worried’ by Guéhi’s gaffes as Aston Villa end City’s flawless start | Manchester City | The Guardian
description: Enzo Maresca is not concerned by the form of Marc Guéhi despite the defender costing his side three goals in the past two Premier League matches
Author: Will Unwin
Headline: Enzo Maresca is not concerned by the form of Marc Guéhi despite the defender costing his side three goals in the past two Premier League matches
Content: Manchester City's Marc Guéhi, flanked by Erling Haaland and goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.Photograph: Martin Rickett/PAView image in fullscreenManchester City's Marc Guéhi, flanked by Erling Haaland and goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma.Photograph: Martin Rickett/PAManchester CityMaresca ‘not worried’ by Guéhi’s gaffes as Aston Villa end City’s flawless startDefender costs three goals in past two league matchesEmery praises ‘fantastic’ match-winner JacksonWill Unwinat Villa ParkSat 24 Oct 2026 11.16 EDTLast modified on Sat 24 Oct 2026 11.33 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleEnzo Maresca is not concerned by the form of Marc Guéhi despite the defender costing his side three goals in the past two Premier League matches, theManchester Citymanager said after seeing his side lose in the league for the first time this season.Nicolas Jackson’s double earned Aston Villaa 2-1 victoryat Villa Park after Guéhi was unable to control the ball for the opener. Instead he spilled it into the path of John McGinn, who played it to Jackson, allowing him to score the first of two goals. The defender was then substituted at half-time having been booked on 32 minutes. Guéhi’s errors allowedIpswich to score twiceagainst City last weekend.Aston Villa and Jackson end Manchester City’s perfect run with stunning winRead more“No, I’m not worried about Marc at all,” Maresca said. “I know that he’s played every minute since the season started with us, with the international team, so it’s not easy. But again, the change was also because he was on a yellow card and in the way we want to be aggressive, sometimes to have one yellow card can be dangerous, but I’m not worried at all.”City had 15 shots to Villa’s eight as they dropped points for the first time this season. Zion Suzuki made a number of important saves to keep City at bay in the second half, and Villa scored with their only two shots on target.“I think we deserved more from the game, for the amount of chances that we created and for the chances that we conceded,” Maresca said. “We lost because probably we have not been clinical enough in their box and sometimes when you concede the first goal because of the mistake, the second goal again comes from transition in 45 minutes. It’s difficult to avoid that every time, but we learn from the game and we try to move on and to improve.”View image in fullscreenNicolas Jackson scores Aston Villa’s first goal past Gianluigi Donnarumma.Photograph: Tony O Brien/ReutersJackson’s double takes him to seven goals since his move from Chelsea. He was a constant threat to the City centre-backs, who were unable to cope with his speed, physical presence and clinical finishing. Unai Emery said of his forward: “He’s very demanding of himself to improve things. Today he scored two goals, in the last matches he scored goals – but at the beginning of the season, what happened to us was more difficult and he was shooting a lot of balls over the corner.“Now, he’s getting better at shooting. He’s working fantastically tactically, he’s understanding as well where we need him. Today, he scored two goals, but the most important thing is how he did his work, his task.”His fellow summer signing Suzuki challenged Jackson for the player of the match award and is starting to show why Villa were so keen to acquire him as Emiliano Martínez’s replacement. Matty Cash told TNT Sport: “He’s brilliant, his first session when he came in, in the possession drill I thought we’d signed a midfielder. His vision is unbelievable, he catches crosses really well which as a full-back is a dream.”Explore more on these topicsManchester CityAston VillaEnzo MarescanewsShareReuse this content

title: European football: Lazio beat Parma to top Serie A; Dortmund lead Bundesliga  | European club football | The Guardian
description: Lazio went three points clear of Serie A champions Inter Milan, and Borussia Dortmund top the Bundesliga after beating Eintracht Frankfurt 1-0
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Lazio went three points clear of Serie A champions Inter Milan, and Borussia Dortmund top the Bundesliga after beating Eintracht Frankfurt 1-0
Content: Lazio’s Kenneth Taylor (right) celebrates his goal against Parma with Tijjani Noslin.Photograph: Fabio Frustaci/EPAView image in fullscreenLazio’s Kenneth Taylor (right) celebrates his goal against Parma with Tijjani Noslin.Photograph: Fabio Frustaci/EPAEuropean club footballEuropean football: Lazio beat Parma to top Serie A; Dortmund lead BundesligaLazio win 2-1 while Roma draw 3-3 with NapoliBeier gives Dortmund win over Eintracht FrankfurtAgence France-PresseSat 24 Oct 2026 17.21 EDTFirst published on Sat 24 Oct 2026 15.27 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleLazioclimbed to the top ofSerie Awith a 2-1 home win ⁠overParma⁠asRoma​twice came from behind to secure a 3-3 draw withNapoliin a pulsating clash in Naples.Lazio have 22 points from their eight matches this ⁠season and are three points clear of champions Inter Milan, who have played a game fewer and host Fiorentina on Sunday. Lazio opened the scoring in the 50th minute as Kenneth Taylor ⁠struck his first of the season, before Parma’s Diego Carlos put the ball into his own net trying ​to cut out a cross. The visitors scored a ‌late consolation through Simone Lontani.Third-placed Roma ‌trailed 2-0 and then 3-2 late on, so will be pleased with a point in Naples as they preserved ‌their 15-game unbeaten league run that dates back to April. Frank Anguissa’s spectacular overhead kick gaveNapolithe lead and Scott McTominay doubled the advantage.At that stage they were cruising, but two goals in four minutes from Matías Soulé and Leonardo Balerdi drewRomalevel. When McTominay added his second in the closing stages the momentum swung back in Napoli’s favour, but Balerdi headed an equaliser for Roma with a minute remaining.Older, calmer, but still playing the hits: Mourinho and Madrid primed for clásicoRead more“We maintained ‌roles, positions and our way of playing,” said the Roma coach, Gian Piero Gasperini. “The goals were of quality. We are fine [with the result], with high morale. Balerdi knows football, has extraordinary ​energy and has been a great signing for us.”Comobacked up their Champions League victory over Manchester United as Anastasios Douvikas scored twice in 11 minutes for a 2-0 win againstSassuolo. They climbed to fourth in the table.In Germany, Maximilian Beier scored in the 80th minute to sendBorussia Dortmundtop of the Bundesliga table after a hard-fought 1-0 home win overEintracht Frankfurt.In a game lacking clear chances, Jobe Bellingham came off the bench and threaded a clever pass for his fellow substitute Beier to score less than a minute later. The narrow victory was Dortmund’s first in the league since mid-September and took Niko Kovac’s side three points clear at the top.Bayern Munich can return to the top with a win at Freiburg on Sunday but will bewithout their coach, Vincent Kompany, who is being treated in hospital for a mystery virus after collapsing at training on Friday.Niclas Füllkrug scored for the sixth straight Bundesliga match asWerder Bremenwon 3-2 atMainz. Füllkrug, who returned to Bremen on loan from West Ham in the summer, converted two penalties inside the opening 25 minutes. Ludovit Reis grabbed Bremen’s other goal, while Anthony Caci and Lee Jae-sung scored for the hosts.View image in fullscreenNiclas Füllkrug (third left) celebrates after scoring his side’s second against Mainz.Photograph: Florian Wiegand/DPA/APRB Leipzigcompleted a comfortable 4-0 home win over promotedElversberg. Romulo scored twice while Tidiam Gomis and Christoph Baumgartner also got on the scoresheet.Paderborn’s Rayan Philippe scored in the 88th minute againstHamburg, his parent club, to grab the promoted side a 1-0 victory.Augsburgdrew 1-1 withUnion Berlinas both sides finished with 10 men.CologneandSchalkeplayed out a scoreless draw in a match marred by a head clash between the visitor’s Robin Gosens and Soufiane El-Faouzi, who left the field after a first-half collision.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionIn La Liga,Atlético Madridkept up the pressure at the top with a 1-0 win overDeportivo A Coruñaat the Riyadh Air Metropolitano. Julián Alvarez struck three minutes into the second half as Diego Simeone’s side extended their unbeaten run to eight matches in all competitions and moved within two points of leaders Barcelona ahead ofEl Clasicoon Sunday.Georges Mikautadze, meanwhile, snatched a late 2-1 win forVillarrealin their derby againstValencia, who had Harvey Elliott sent off as both sides finished with 10 men. The visitors came from behind to triumph, leaving Javier Aguirre’s side 19th.View image in fullscreenHarvey Elliott, on loan at Valencia from Liverpool, was sent off in the 89th minute against Villarreal.Photograph: Maria Jose Segovia/DeFodi Images/ShutterstockPepelu putValenciaahead from the penalty spot in the first half before the American defender Alex Freeman headed the visitors level after 69 minutes. Iñigo Pérez’s Villarreal had Pape Gueye sent off when the Senegal international hit José Gayà in the face with his elbow.However, Elliott, who is on loan from Liverpool, was soon dismissed for two quick yellow cards for apparent dissent. Mikautadze broke through in stoppage time, racing through and finishing with aplomb to claim the three points.In France,Lenscame from behind to beatParis FC2-1 ⁠with Thorgan Hazard’s 83rd-minute winner taking them to within a point of the Ligue 1 leaders. Lens, who ⁠were runners-up last season, ⁠made ​a slow start to the season and fired coach Dino Toppmöller after six matches in charge, but under ⁠Yannick Cahuzac they have won successive French league games to advance to 13 points from eight matches. They are one ⁠point behind five clubs who share the lead on 14, including Paris ​FC.Explore more on these topicsEuropean club footballSerie ANapoliRomaBorussia DortmundEintracht FrankfurtBundesliganewsShareReuse this content

title: Burnley sack Nicky Hayen after Lincoln rout leaves them in bottom three | Burnley | The Guardian
description: Nicky Hayen has left Burnley after only 14 games in charge following a 4-1 defeat at Lincoln that left a team expected to challenge for promotion in relegation danger
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: Nicky Hayen has left Burnley after only 14 games in charge following a 4-1 defeat at Lincoln that left a team expected to challenge for promotion in relegation danger
Content: The 4-1 defeat at Lincoln proved to be Nicky Hayen’s last in charge of Burnley.Photograph: Lee Keuneke/PAView image in fullscreenThe 4-1 defeat at Lincoln proved to be Nicky Hayen’s last in charge of Burnley.Photograph: Lee Keuneke/PABurnleyBurnley sack Nicky Hayen after Lincoln rout leaves them in bottom threeBelgian won only one of his 14 games in chargeRelegated Burnley expected to challenge for promotionGuardian sportSat 24 Oct 2026 14.05 EDTLast modified on Sat 24 Oct 2026 16.17 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleBurnley have sacked Nicky Hayen after only 14 games in charge, in the wake of a 4-1 defeat at Lincoln that left the Clarets in the Championship’s relegation zone.The Belgian was appointed in the summer as the permanent successor to Scott Parker, who left in April with relegation from the Premier League inevitable. He leaves having won just one match, a 4-0 league victory at Watford on 10 October.Championship roundup: Southampton beat West Ham; QPR put five past SwanseaRead moreBurnley edged past Notts County on penalties in the Carabao Cup in his first match in charge and recovered in the last seven minutes from 2-0 down to draw at home to West Ham in their opening game of the Championship season. However, they then lost badly at West Brom and Norwich, sandwiching a shootout exit from the Carabao Cup at Bradford, and the pattern was set.Burnley were fancied to push for promotion, which was achieved in their past two Championship seasons, but are now at risk of relegation. Wolves’ come-from-behind win at Turf Moor last weekend left Hayen on the brink and now the club have acted.A terse, two-sentence statement on the club website said: “Burnley Football Club has dismissed head coach Nicky Hayen with immediate effect. The board has taken the decision following a disappointing start to the Championship season.”Hayen had earlier said in his post-match press conference, before news of his dismissal emerged: “It’s frustrating for everyone, especially the fans. I want to apologise to them, but I know it doesn’t matter because it’s another hard defeat for them and I can understand their criticism.“We haven’t got the results. I will keep on working hard as long as I have the chance. But there will be a day if it carries on like this that it stops. I know it’s a really tough defeat and something to think about for the board.”Explore more on these topicsBurnleyChampionshipnewsShareReuse this content

title: Scottish Premiership: Kelsy fires Rangers to emphatic win; Dundee United pip Aberdeen | Scottish Premiership | The Guardian
description: Kevin Kelsy scored two goals to help Rangers to a 4-0 win over 10-man St Johnstone in the Scottish Premiership while Dundee United beat Aberdeen 3-2
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Kevin Kelsy scored two goals to help Rangers to a 4-0 win over 10-man St Johnstone in the Scottish Premiership while Dundee United beat Aberdeen 3-2
Content: Rangers’ Ryan Naderi (right) scores their first goal at a rain-swept Ibrox.Photograph: Steve Welsh/PAView image in fullscreenRangers’ Ryan Naderi (right) scores their first goal at a rain-swept Ibrox.Photograph: Steve Welsh/PAScottish PremiershipScottish Premiership: Kelsy fires Rangers to emphatic win; Dundee United pip AberdeenRangers 4-0 St Johnstone; Dundee United 3-2 AberdeenKevin Kelsy scores two to sink 10-man SaintsPress AssociationSat 24 Oct 2026 12.52 EDTLast modified on Sat 24 Oct 2026 15.20 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleDerek McInnes asked hisRangersside to be “brilliant” againstSt Johnstoneand was rewarded with a 4-0 Premiership win at Ibrox. Afterdropping two points at Dundee last Saturday, the Light Blues dominated the first half but only led at the interval through a goal in the 29th minute from the Venezuela forward Kevin Kelsy.Saints started the second half brightly but goals from the Gers striker Ryan Naderi in the 61st minute and Kelsy again five minutes later had the home side cruising. The Saints substitute Kai Fotheringham was shown a straight red card by Chris Graham in the 74th minute for his high challenge on the midfielder Nico Raskin, before the substitute Tochi Chukwuani added a fourth for the hosts with three minutes remaining.Older, calmer, but still playing the hits: Mourinho and Madrid primed for clásicoRead moreMcInnes said: “It’s quite ironic in the sense that we were so good and so brilliant at times in the first half and create so many opportunities, that we were only a goal to the good at half-time. And obviously, we don’t want to let the frustration of those missed opportunities and dominance filter into the second half.“I think half-time came at a bad time for us because, despite the conditions, some of the play was really good. I asked the players to be brilliant today, not just win the game, can we really commit to being the best we can be, as good as we can be? And I thought we were in the first half. Everything was brilliant except the result at half-time because we should have been more in in front.”Celticcan restore their four-point advantage overRangersat the top when they travel toHibernian, the bottom side, at noon GMT on Sunday.Dundee Unitedwon a rollercoaster game 3-2 againstAberdeenat Tannadice. Zidane Iqbal scored for the hosts before the visitors equalised through Nesta Guinness-Walker – both players scoring their first goals for their clubs.United took the lead once more thanks to a Dylan Tait strike, with Connor Ronan drawingAberdeenlevel after the break. Zac Sapsford secured all three points for his side, with the win moving United up to fourth – one point behindHearts, who are atMotherwellon Sunday – while Aberdeen dropped to ninth.Two own goals helpedFalkirkclimb to seventh with a 3-0 victory overKilmarnock. Centre-backs Cathal McCarthy and George Stanger scored past their own goalkeeper either side of a Jacob Murrell header.St Mirrenended their losing streak with a 2-1 victory overDundeewith goals from Calvin Ramsay and Eseosa Sule before Bradley Fink pulled one back for the visitors.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionThis story will be updated after Sunday’s matchesExplore more on these topicsScottish PremiershipRangersSt JohnstoneDundee UnitedAberdeenFalkirkKilmarnocknewsShareReuse this content

title: Why Stanley Matthews’ Ballon d’Or triumph echoes down the years for Harry Kane | Harry Kane | The Guardian
description: In 1956, the Blackpool great was recognised for his force of individual will, the very thing that makes the Bayern and England striker the standout candiate
Author: Jonathan Wilson
Headline: In 1956, the Blackpool great was recognised for his force of individual will, the very thing that makes the Bayern and England striker the standout candiate
Content: An England fan holds up a sign saying ‘Harry's #1 fan’. The Bayern Munich and Three Lions striker’s consistency and longevity are compelling reasons for him to be this year’s Ballon d’Or winner.Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenAn England fan holds up a sign saying ‘Harry's #1 fan’. The Bayern Munich and Three Lions striker’s consistency and longevity are compelling reasons for him to be this year’s Ballon d’Or winner.Photograph: Catherine Ivill/AMA/Getty ImagesInside footballHarry KaneWhy Stanley Matthews’ Ballon d’Or triumph echoes down the years for Harry KaneJonathan WilsonIn 1956, the Blackpool great was recognised for his force of individual will, the very thing that makes the Bayern and England striker the standout candiateSat 24 Oct 2026 15.00 EDTLast modified on Sat 24 Oct 2026 18.22 EDTShareSystems football began In 1963(On the hallowed turf at Wembley)With the impact of a cynical foulBy Gino Pivatelli.At that moment in the European Cup final, when the hard-working Milan forward, brought in to combat Benfica’s Mário Coluna, caught the great playmaker, football of the individual came to an end. The foul not only checked a promising break, but broke a bone in Coluna’s foot. Without substitutes, he hobbled on, diminished, and Milan won 2-1 to lift the trophy and register the first victory for a team that prioritised the system over the individual. Modern football was born.There are degrees, of course. The success of Zinedine Zidane’s Real Madrid was far more predicated on individuals than that of, say, Thomas Tuchel’s Chelsea or Pep Guardiola’s Manchester City. But, fundamentally, since that first success forcatenaccio, football has been resolutely a team game.Which is what always makes individual awards in the game such an oddity. Even in successful teams there is often a tension between the individual and the collective. That can be productive – sparks of friction are often creative. In sides that disappoint, though, the issue, whether the result of his own ego or the shortcomings of his teammates, is often an overreliance on one individual.View image in fullscreenStanley Matthews was the first Ballon d’Or winner despite his club Blackpool’s relative lack of success.Photograph: Hulton Archive/Getty ImagesWhen the Ballon d’Or launched in 1956, that paradox was less pronounced. If the decision back then was less contentious than Monday’s award will assuredly be, though, it can only have been because there was no social media on which the furious could vent.That the Hungarian vote was split between Ferenc Puskás, József Bozsik and Sándor Kocsis immediately highlighted a problem that successful teams still face, although given the award was made a month after the uprising was crushed by and Soviet tanks entering Budapest, with two of the three players in the process of defecting, it was probably just as well for the magazine France Football that none of the Hungarians did triumph.Still, the choice ofStanley Matthews, from today’s perspective, looks odd. While it is true Blackpool had finished second in the First Division in 1956, but they were 11 points behind Manchester United and had gone out of the FA Cup in the third round. Was there not a case for Duncan Edwards or Tommy Taylor? Or for Bert Trautmann, the goalkeeper who won the Football Writers’ player of the year in 1956 after playing on with a broken neck in the final as Manchester City lifted the Cup?Looking beyond England, what ofAlfredo Di Stéfano, who had inspired Real Madrid to the inaugural European Cup? Or one of the Athletic Bilbao players who had just won La Liga? Or Pivatelli, who had been top-scorer in Serie A? Or Giuliano Sarti, the goalkeeper who had won the Scudetto with Fiorentina? Or Nikita Simonyan, whose goals had powered Spartak Moscow to the Soviet title? Matthews was 38, and there’s a clear sense that the inaugural Ballon d’Or was something of a lifetime achievement award.Perhaps that is fine. Maybe the award should recognise longevity. What, after all, is it for? It’s certainly not just about how much a player wins in a given year. If it were, Fabián Ruiz would be a hot favourite on Monday, having won the World Cup, the Champions League and Ligue 1 this season.Yet fine player though the midfielder undoubtedly is, he would be neither Paris Saint-Germain nor Spain’s player of the season. Besides, an award for winning lots of other awards is the definition of gilding the lily. There’s perhaps even an argument that individual awards represent an opportunity to acknowledge those who strive and delight but rarely win medals.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionChaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan LiewRead moreAccording to its website, the Ballon d’Or is “awarded based on three essential pillars … individual performance, team achievements, and class combined with fair play.” The “complete” winner will be defined by a “combination of talent, sportsmanship and competitive excellence”.Team achievement is perhaps easiest to isolate. PSG have largely ditched their egos as Luis Enrique has led them to back-to-back Champions Leagues, but how do you tease out which of their exceptional front three has been the most important?Ousmane Dembélé won that battle last year. Khvicha Kvaratskhelia was arguably the standout this year, but, in a World Cup year, can a player whose country didn’t qualify be regarded as the best individual? And neither Dembélé nor the other member of the trio, Desiré Doué, had an especially notable World Cup.Given the relative level of the French league and the fact PSG can rest players for domestic games to keep them fresh for Europe, it’s arguable the greatest achievement by a European club last season came from Arsenal, as they won the Premier League and reached the Champions League final. But their strength is the collective, and only three of the 30-man shortlist are Arsenal players, but none of Gabriel, William Saliba or Declan Rice had stellar World Cups.What then of Spain? They too are a team short on star quality, certainly when Lamine Yamal is carrying an injury as he did for the first few months of this year. They won the World Cup, ultimately, because of the collective strength of their midfield. Rodri is the embodiment of their approach, but his involvement at Manchester City in the second half of last season was restricted.View image in fullscreenBayern Munich’s Harry Kane heads home against Stuttgart: 61 in 51 club games last season represents a remarkable record.Photograph: Annegret Hilse/ReutersReal Madrid have just endured one of only five trophyless seasons this century, which weakens the claims of Kylian Mbappé and Jude Bellingham and Vinícius. Lionel Messi had great moments at the World Cup but playing in MLS reduces his chances. Which perhaps means it’s time again to reward somebody who has had a good year, even if he went out of the World Cup in the semis and the Champions League in the quarters:Harry Kane.Goals in the Bundesliga may not quite have the currency they did when Karl-Heinz Rummenigge was scoring them, but 61 in 51 club games last season represents a remarkable record, and he also got six at the World Cup, winning the game against the Democratic Republic of the Congo almost by force of individual will.In a season without an obvious outstanding candidate, there seems a strong possibility that the panel, just as it did in 1956, will reward consistency and longevity.Explore more on these topicsHarry KaneInside footballEnglandBayern MunichBallon d'OrcommentShareReuse this content

Content: 2h ago18.53 EDTGiles Richards' reportAnd here is Giles’s verdict:double quotation markAntonelli’s first pole since the Belgian GP in July could not have been better timed as he attempts to take his first title.
